correctness.rationale: A retraction onto a two-dimensional subalgebra forces a nonzero square-zero element with nonzero cotangent part. Odd characteristic forces a single nonzero linear coordinate. The decomposition A=A' ⊕ x_i A' and invertibility of its normalized coefficient gives the unique pivot normal form. Explicit substitution gives every map, its rank, and each image fiber. Tangent maps of full automorphisms are monomial, so support cardinality classifies the d orbits. Generatorwise evaluation yields the necessary and sufficient commuting condition; counting zero off-pivot coefficients gives the degree enumerator, ordered pair, edge, isolation and clique formulas. The exact standalone checker exhausts all unital endomorphisms at (d,q)=(2,3),(2,5) and all parametrized pairs at (3,3). It is corroboration rather than infinity proof. No independent audit is claimed.

originality.rationale: The specific claim is a full automorphism-orbit and commuting-graph degree classification for image-dimension-two unital algebra retractions of square-zero variable complete intersections over odd finite fields. Díaz et al. treat characteristic-zero automorphism groups, not this rank-two idempotent monoid or commuting graph. The closest published-finding corpus full-text statement treats all ranks but characteristic two, with one rank-two orbit rather than d odd-characteristic orbit classes. Another inspected published-finding corpus theorem concerns automorphism tangent groups at prime-power exponents, not rank-two retractions. The earlier graded-retract classification does not by itself imply the full non-graded combinatorial and commuting-degree result. Five named targeted semantic searches recovered these but no direct match; this is evidence, not absolute novelty proof. value.rationale: The two-dimensional-image retracts are the minimal proper nontrivial split subalgebras of an infinite family of nonreduced monomial complete intersections. The exact orbit census and explicit commuting graph give the unexpected structural reconstruction property that the combinatorially defined graph degree detects a full algebraic automorphism-conjugacy orbit. This separates the odd-field d-type pattern sharply from the characteristic-two single rank-two orbit and supplies exact graph-theoretic invariants over all odd finite fields and all d>=2. It is a complete natural invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice; no downstream theorem is asserted.
